title: Binary integrity pins
description: Which Core binary the Connector is allowed to execute, and how it proves that. Xray is never bundled into the extension archive and never vendored in git (ADR-0019): it is fetched at first run and validated against this document. A mismatch is IntegrityMismatch and means refusing to start, because a binary nobody pinned is the one place a supply-chain compromise becomes a proxy that carries your users' traffic.

pinsVersion.description: Version of this pins document, so the Connector can tell a stale local copy from a deliberately older pin.

releaseTag.description: Exact tag, never a range or 'latest'.

signaturePubkey.description: Minisign trusted public key for the release signature. Null is allowed only when sha256 pinning is in force and documented as the sole control.

upstream.description: Where the binary comes from. Exactly one repository is expressible; mirrors are not.

verifySignature.description: Hash pinning alone proves nothing if the attacker controls both the asset and the list. Signature verification is required, not optional.

silentSelfUpdate.description: Core updates happen only on explicit user action, with re-verification and the previous version retained for rollback (docs/architecture/33).

installRoot.description: Per-user path resolved by the Connector, e.g. %LOCALAPPDATA%\NEXORA\core. Not in the extension directory, not in Program Files: no elevation, and the ACL stays user-owned.

retainedPreviousVersions.description: How many prior verified cores to keep for rollback. Zero means an upgrade cannot be undone without a re-download.

assets.description: One entry per OS/arch the Connector may fetch. An absent platform is a refusal to run there, not a fallback.

url.description: Only the pinned upstream release host. A mirror is a supply-chain decision and is not expressible here.

verifiedAt.description: When a human or CI actually checked this pin against upstream. A pin nobody verified is a pin that drifted.

authenticodeSubject.description: Windows only. Recorded because unsigned binaries trip antivirus heuristics; the observation belongs in the pin, not in a support ticket (docs/architecture/33).

then.description: Unreachable guard: if no release key is pinned, per-asset signatures become mandatory.
